request: Analyze GSE144109 for PMID 33332990 (Exercise during pregnancy mitigates negative effects of parental obesity on metabolic function in adult mouse offspring.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina TruSeq stranded total RNA, HiSeq 2500), quadriceps of adult female offspring

grp: MHE (maternal HF, dam ran voluntarily during gestation)
PHE (paternal HF, dam ran during gestation)

final.inclusion: 15 female offspring, n=3 per group (GEO overall design: '3 samples per groups'); NC-Sed shared control for maternal (Study 1) and paternal (Study 2) lines (GEO treatment protocol)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of maternal voluntary wheel running during gestation on adult female offspring skeletal-muscle transcriptome under parental high-fat diet: MHE vs MHS (maternal HF line) and PHE vs PHS (paternal HF line)
planned_contrasts: grp_MHE_vs_MHS: maternal exercise within maternal-HF line (abstract: 'maternal exercise resulted in a transcriptional profile similar to offspring from NC-fed parents'; paper count not in abstract)
grp_PHE_vs_PHS: maternal exercise within paternal-HF line (same abstract sentence)
grp_MHS_vs_NCS and grp_PHS_vs_NCS: parental HF vs NC (abstract: profiles 'enriched in genes regulating inflammation and immune responses')
grp_MHE_vs_NCS and grp_PHE_vs_NCS: does exercise bring HF offspring back toward NC (abstract: 'similar to NC')
final.paper_method: DESeq2 v1.11.8 'for maternal and paternal lines separately' (GEO data_processing; full methods not available)
final.paper_results: Abstract: HF (maternal or paternal) offspring muscle enriched in inflammation/immune genes; maternal exercise gave a profile similar to NC offspring. No DEG counts or named genes in the abstract (Pgc-1a named only for promoter methylation).

alignment.reasoning: inspect alignment_keys: title matches 15/15 matrix columns exactly. grp is taken from the GEO 'group' characteristic (NCS/MHS/MHE/PHS/PHE), consistent with the diet/treatment/parent columns.

matrix.reasoning: Deposited file is DESeq2-normalized featureCounts counts (data_processing: 'gene coverages in units of normalized read counts'; 61.6% integer). Each column is exactly integer counts / size factor: multiplying by 1/(smallest positive value) gives integers with max deviation 1e-8 on all 50,686 genes x 15 samples (prep_counts.py). This is an exact inversion, not rounding of estimated counts; recovered library sizes 18-27M reads are plausible for 100-bp SE HiSeq. The reconstructed integers equal the featureCounts counts up to one per-sample constant, which DESeq2's size-factor estimation removes. Paper input: DESeq2 on featureCounts counts, so the matrix agrees with the paper.

candidates.reason_rejected: the matrix is exactly invertible to counts, so the paper's count route is available

design.reasoning: The exercise estimand is maternal running vs sedentary within the same parental-HF exposure: MHE vs MHS and PHE vs PHS (primary). HF vs NC and HF-Ex vs NC test the abstract's 'inflammation' and 'similar to NC' statements (secondary). There is no NC-Ex arm, so the exercise effect under normal chow and an exercise x diet interaction cannot be estimated; the five groups are levels of one factor, not a full factorial. Following GEO data_processing ('DESeq2 ... for maternal and paternal lines separately'), each line is fitted on its own three groups with the shared NCS controls. n=3 per arm.
